title: Running on Empty
summary: One of Alhaji Musa's six kekes is eating fuel money. His spreadsheet blames the wrong one. Find the keke that's really costing him.

client.name: Alhaji Musa
brief: I log every fuel fill-up and every repair for my six tricycles. One of them is costing me far more per kilometre than the others — I want to know which, before I sell the wrong one.
Some days the driver forgets to write the odometer reading. Don't let that throw you off, and don't let one repair bill fool you either.
client.thanks: KK-04, not KK-02! I was about to sell the wrong keke. That repair bill had me completely fooled. Thank you.

starterSql:
-- Musa Keke Fleet: which keke really costs the most to run, per kilometre?
-- keke_log mixes fuel fill-ups and repair bills; some days have no odometer reading.

SELECT *
FROM keke_log
LIMIT 20;

tables.name: keke_log
tables.description: Every fuel fill-up and repair logged for the six-keke fleet.

columns.name: litres
columns.desc: Litres bought (fuel rows only; blank for repairs)

columns.name: distance_km
columns.desc: Odometer distance since the last entry (blank on days the driver forgot to log it)

hints.title: Hint 1: Two different kinds of cost
hints.desc: A repair bill is real money, but it isn't fuel cost, and folding it into a cost-per-km figure makes an otherwise-efficient keke look terrible for one day.

hints.title: Hint 2: Filter before you divide
hints.desc: Only use fuel rows with a logged distance when working out cost per kilometre.
hints.snippet: WHERE category = 'fuel' AND distance_km IS NOT NULL

hints.title: Hint 3: Shape of the answer
hints.desc: Sum fuel cost and sum distance per keke, divide one by the other, and find the keke with the highest ratio.

findings.claim: Which keke genuinely costs the most to run per kilometre, and should be looked at first?

options.text: KK-02 — its running costs are far above the rest of the fleet
KK-04 — once the repair bill is set aside, its fuel cost per km is the real outlier
None of them — every keke costs roughly the same to run

findings.claim: Why did the fleet spreadsheet point at the wrong keke?

options.text: A single repair bill was averaged in with fuel costs, inflating that keke's apparent running cost for one day.
Fuel prices went up sharply that week, affecting every keke equally.
A driver has been siphoning fuel to sell.

successFeedback: KK-02's number was a cracked-axle repair bill, not fuel. Once that's set aside, KK-04 is the one quietly burning naira — its engine needs a service, not a sale.

fixtures.failHint: Your answer doesn't match the fleet's logged costs and distances.

fixtures.purpose: A week with more missing odometer readings and a heavy repair bill
fixtures.failHint: A repair bill isn't a fuel cost, and a day with no odometer reading can't be divided into — leave both out.

fixtures.purpose: A smaller fleet with no repair noise, to check the ratio itself is right
fixtures.failHint: Check your cost-per-km formula on a fleet with no repair bills to distract from.

fixtures.purpose: A fleet where nobody has had a repair yet
fixtures.failHint: With no repair rows at all, your filter should still pick out the right keke.

evidence.title: A mechanic's invoice
evidence.text: Found clipped to Alhaji Musa's fuel ledger: "INVOICE — KK-02, cracked rear axle, parts and labour: ₦48,000. Paid 18/11." Someone had copied this straight into the same column as the fuel receipts.
